findings.evidence: T1 design.md, section "No mergeability": "GitHub `mergeable` is not read." `template/scripts/publication_queue.py` `_prepare` detects the conflict through `merge_conflicts(root, head, current_main)`. The new tests only cover merge-tree conflicts: `test_conflict_outside_generated_files_needs_integration_repair` and `test_unavailable_derived_merge_with_a_real_conflict_needs_integration_repair`. A candidate that GitHub reports as CONFLICTING but that is never selected by `_worker_candidate` still shows only the generic checks reason. The narrowing was recorded as a coordinator decision (variant A) in the proposal, so I am reporting it as an outcome-coverage note, not a defect.
findings.summary: Requirement item 3 is stated in terms of GitHub `mergeable=CONFLICTING`. The implementation never reads GitHub mergeability. It routes a conflict to integration repair only when `_prepare` runs `merge-tree` during `_integrate`, and that happens only when the worker picks the candidate up.

findings.evidence: `template/scripts/task_content_identity.py` `main_only_integration`: `differing = {path for path in diff.stdout.split("\0") if path} - generated`. The T2 design.md says: "Generated content is validated by its own `--check`, as today." This is consistent with the regeneration added in `execute_integration_repair`. Verification that generated files stay current therefore depends on a different component than the one that decides to reuse the receipt.
findings.summary: `main_only_integration` excludes every path in the generated set from both the conflict check and the final tree diff. A change to a generated file therefore never invalidates the receipt through this proof. It relies on the separate `--check` of generated files and on the new `regenerate_declared_files` step in integration repair. If a generated file also carried hand-written content, the proof would not notice.
